reaction_equations: ½S/C138 : OH/C3 + Zn(CH2CH3)2 ! ½S/C138 : OZn(CH2CH3)2/C3 + C2H6
½S/C138 : OZn(CH2CH3)2/C3 + H2O ! ½S/C138 : OZnOH/C3 + C2H6
surface_mechanism_description: The ALD process involves two half-reactions: first, the surface hydroxyl groups react with diethylzinc (DEZ) to form surface-alkylated zinc species and ethane, followed by the reaction of the surface-alkylated zinc species with water to form surface-alkoxide zinc species and ethane. These reactions occur on the particle substrate and are followed by purge steps to prevent gas-phase side reactions.
evidence: The binary CVD reaction for ZnO deposition is: Zn(CH2CH3)2 + H2O ! ZnO + 2C2H6 (1). Equation 1 can be separated into two ALD half-reactions: [S/C138 : OH/C3 + Zn(CH2CH3)2 ! [S/C138 : OZn(CH2CH3)2/C3 + C2H6 (2) and [S/C138 : OZn(CH2CH3)2/C3 + H2O ! [S/C138 : OZnOH/C3 + C2H6 (3) which occur solely on the particle substrate, [S], and are each followed by inert (typically N2 or argon) purge steps to prevent unwanted gas-phase side reactions that are normally associated with CVD processes.
